utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, this is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Before we start, is there anything that both parties want to address to this Court? Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, Mr. President, Your Honours, I won't take long. What is it about? Last week, both Defences applied for a short break when Mr. Krsnik finishes examining the witnesses who are here in The Hague before the departure to Mostar, because it was envisaged to take the depositions in Mostar. Now we are faced with a new situation. We have your decision that these witnesses will be heard in The Hague and will be giving the deposition in The Hague. We also have Mr. Krsnik's and Mr. Meek's brief saying that they are giving up the examination of witnesses through depositions and now we have a new situation. In this brief, as far as I can see, asked that some deadlines be moved, the possibility to examine the witnesses by videolink, the possibility of examining these witnesses after Mr. Martinovic's defence starts calling its witnesses. Your Honours, this Defence, the Vinko Martinovic's Defence, today, you will get our application in which we are asking for a break so that we can keep a normal pace, whilst preparing our case, and rounding off our defence, namely I have talked with Mr. Krsnik and they believe that they will finish examining the witnesses who are in The Hague on Tuesday, that is the 2nd of July, and as they've renounced the depositions, it means that we would find ourselves in a predicament because we should -- we would then be expected to embark on our case on the 3rd of July. Your Honours, would it be possible, as I have said you will receive our application today, could we start on the 15th of July? We need this break because we really need to bring our preparations to a proper end, to proof our witnesses, we have to organise our -- their arrival and we would be able to begin on the 15th of July. So all that we are asking for is a short break between the 2nd and the 12th of July. You will have our application today. And then we could start on the 15th of July and then we could work without any further intermission until the summer recess. Mr. Krsnik also wishes to say something. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I will also be very brief. After your decision that we could not get the depositions in Mostar, this Defence has some suggestions, in view of the deadline for this case. You know that I cannot provide witnesses after the 2nd of July because this is impossible, I've already said that. They either don't have passports or Dutch visas or are sick so that from the 2nd of July onward I simply cannot get any witness here in The Hague. Your Honours, I will once again went through the list of depositions and I believe we shall renounce calling certain witnesses because they might be repetitious so that it will look more or less like this. We will bring four witnesses to testify in the courtroom, Your Honours, and then two or three or four we would organise the videolink for these four witnesses, who will be coming and testifying in the Court, they are not long, we can start on the 15th and finish them on the 16th of July, and then all that we would have to do would be the videolink at the time that you decide. And then we would, I believe, fit into all the deadlines, and I do not think that we would lose much. And the videolink could be organised immediately after the recess, that is after Mr. Seric begins his case. I think this is sensible suggestion and I believe everybody will understand it. We will not be wasting any time. The viva voce witnesses will then be finished by the 17th of July and then we would have two, three or maybe four at the outside videolink witnesses and then we do it straight away after the summer break before Mr. Seric resumes. They could be finished in two days and that would be it. Otherwise, Mr. Naletilic's Defence will be in a serious predicament because it has failed to produce its witnesses. And we have been thinking about the solution and decided that perhaps it would best serve the purpose both of the Defence and the Chamber and we believe that the Prosecution will not have anything against it, and if all my other witnesses here finish by the 2nd of July, I hope my learned friends will not take too much time cross-examining them so on Tuesday we would finish those witnesses, there will be a short break for Mr. Seric on the 15th, I have my two witnesses, I finish with them and that's it and then we only need two or perhaps three days at the most for our videolinks. Thank you very much, Your Honours. I believe this is a sensible suggestion. I believe it will be acceptable to Your Honours and acceptable to the Prosecution. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for informing us of your plan. As we said before, that the cancellation of the deposition is also a shock to this Chamber. We will do everything possible to accommodate your request. Let me hear Mr. Scott. Is it on this subject, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we appreciate the additional information because frankly it's been very unclear to us what the schedule would be over the next few weeks as well. I must say I'm not convinced that we will be finished by next Tuesday, because there appear to be still substantial number of against witnesses ahead of us and I learned yesterday that if it's correct that Mr. Krsnik intends to call the two remaining expert witnesses next week. So that puts at least, I don't know, some five or six perhaps even seven additional witnesses in front of us so I'm not -- can't say that I'm particularly optimistic that we will finish by Tuesday. That's simply an observation. In terms of the four witnesses which Mr. Krsnik proposes to call live, appreciating the fact that there has been some recent changes in the schedule it's not clear to me why we couldn't do those the week of the 8th of July and cover those four witnesses who presumably there seems to be some indication he is able to get them to the Hague live, which I assume that means they have the appropriate travel papers, et cetera. So not entirely clear to me why they could not come and we could finish them sooner. Again as we have said before, I have no objection in principle, the Prosecution has no objection in concept, to some short pause to allow the Martinovic Defence to organise itself. We understand that and that's make that clear. Again the concept we said before we are not opposed to that. But it seems to me that perhaps the cleaner way to do this, our observation would be, Mr. President, would be to try to finish the four additional live Tuta Defence witnesses as soon as possible, and then take, if the Court -- if the Chamber is so inclined, then take a break before the Martinovic case. That's point number 2. Point number 3 just perhaps by way of clarification, if I understand what Mr. Krsnik is proposing, these three or four remaining videolink witnesses would be taken after the August recess, if -- and I guess I'm asking to clarify that. That's what I thought I heard him say at one point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik? Would you please answer this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we've studied it very thoroughly, trying to meet all the requests of the Chamber, of the schedule and so on and so forth, and we thought it would be best because we heard that the Tribunal will be having a plenary and if we finished on Tuesday and I hope we will be able to do that, I hope our learned friend, Mr. Scott, understands that with the experts, I have another seven witnesses. Today is Wednesday so it's yet -- it's eight days and they are not long witnesses. You can see from the summaries. So I do not see what would have to happen to prevent us from finishing on Tuesday or Wednesday, even though the cross-examination takes more than twice as much time as the direct examination but never mind that. So we thought if we finish on Wednesday, which is the 2nd or the 3rd of July, and then we would have a break until the 15th of July, and then break, if I understood you, you would be glad to have this break. During that break, Mr. Seric would get ready and we could start on the 15th, except that I would be the one to start again with those four witnesses. And it sounds very sensible to me. On the 15th of July. Because I really cannot get the witnesses earlier than that. Mr. Scott has been in the Tribunal for a long time and he knows how the witnesses unit works and what problems there are with passports and all the rest, and who never thought they would never be coming here because they never thought they would have to come. As for the videolink we have been informed by the registry that until they have carried out all the checks and possibilities and so on and so forth to have the videolink from Mostar that we cannot set the dates, so that is why I said I do not know when but we can do it during a break after Mr. Seric sets off. If there is a need for all this haste. If not, then it can all be -- then we finish, then we can take it until the -- until the recess, that is I will take during the month of July, with the videolinks and everything else, and perhaps that will be the thing that would make me the happiest. Because I think, to begin with, I know that I carried out all the preparations for the next stage and also to take a breath, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I'll give the floor to Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In light of these discussions, I know that I can give you the following information. We are actively trying to accommodate you in that you can have your videolinks and things like that but I know so far that the videolink in Mostar won't be possible, it would only be possible in Zagreb or Sarajevo. So it's -- and we can discuss this after the session. We can make an appointment to discuss this further in detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, up to now we haven't received any written submissions from the Defence counsel yet so we will act in accordance with the schedule we made for this case, but there are two points I would like to stress. That is as I said before, that this Trial Chamber is also shocked by the cancellation of the deposition in Mostar, which means that there are a lot of rescheduling and reallocation of resources in this aspect, which involves a lot of logistic preparations for the continuation of this case in The Hague. Secondly, we believe that Mr. Martinovic's case has to start on the 15th of July, as we clearly stated in our decisions before. So I hope we could finish the live witnesses in two weeks' time, which means this week and next week. So if there is any time, especially during the week from the 8th to the 12th, we will have a short break. Because during that time, first, there will be a plenary planned on the 10th, 11th and 12th. Secondly there will be an annual musical festival in the conference centre in front of this building, which means it will be very difficult to bring any witness and the accused to the courtroom. So we will make a break during that week. As for how long the break will be, it's very difficult Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to say at this moment, because we have to finish all the witnesses before that. Any way, we will make decisions, written decisions, after we have received the written submissions from the Defence counsel. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, those submissions were filed yesterday afternoon, so you should have those sometime today. I have an objection on a different issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: My objection, Your Honour, goes to the cross-examination by Mr. Stringer of this witness. It has gone on now for much longer than the direct examination. The points covered on the direct examination have been fully covered by Mr. Stringer. I was called to the carpet for being on fishing expeditions several times in my cross-examination of some Prosecution witnesses. I think Mr. Stringer is on a field trip right now with this witness. This is an interrogation. It's no longer cross-examination. And for the record, we object, Your Honours. We believe there has to be some time limit and you've got to rope Mr. Stringer in to the issues. I mean this witness has said within the first five minutes, yes he signed those orders, why do we spend another 45 minutes having him say the same thing? I really do object, Your Honours, to this tactic on the part of the Prosecution to do an investigation through a cross-examination of this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, it is our intention to have our next witness during the next sitting, and would you please brief us how long are you going to take for the present witness this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at the beginning of the cross-examination, I distributed a list of the exhibits that I proposed to put in front of the witness in the order, and we are down to Exhibit P619.1, and so I hope to go through those remaining exhibits, I believe I can do so rapidly. I would submit that we have managed to cover a lot of territory in a reasonable amount of time. I respectfully disagree with counsel that this has been a fishing expedition. It's our submission that these issues go to a number, not only the witness's direct testimony but a number of issues that are central to the case and that will continue in the exhibits that I propose to review with him today. But I'm confident that I can do this swiftly. I believe I've done so up to this point. And I will move rapidly through the remaining exhibits, I'm confident that we can finish this by the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Just so long as the record reflects our objection to the Prosecution having a more than twice the amount of time that we took on direct examination. Just so long as the record reflects a contemporaneous objection and a continuing one also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, I believe that is your allegation. You understand that the Registrar calculated the time. We have to act in accordance with the time calculated by the Registrar. Well, we are very interested to hear the cross-examination. I believe that Mr. Stringer did a very good job yesterday to go over a lot of documents in that two bundles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, those two binders are the same two binders essentially that Your Honours would not admit into evidence in January. So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, I think there will be some other reasons for not admitting those documents into the evidence. It's not because the contents of those documents, it's because the late submission of those documents, and as a principle of this trial, all these documents, if you want to have them admitted, they have to go through the witness. Anyway, we'll hear what Mr. Stringer is going to cross-examine that witness on. Could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll speak very loudly because the microphone is over there so I don't have to fiddle with the microphone. Just while the witness is coming in, can I confirm then, because I think it's important frankly for everyone's schedule and purposes, that in any event because of the plenary there will be no court or depositions on the 10th, 11th or 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there might be depositions if Mr. Krsnik is still wanting that deposition process.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's my understanding this morning that the deposition process had gone away completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I heard that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we won't take long this morning. Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'd ask the witness be shown Exhibit 607.2, which is an exhibit we were looking at yesterday. I can inform the usher we are also going to move rapidly to the next three documents that are on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the document that's been placed in front of you? Do you recognise it from yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is a report from Mr. Bozic, who is the warden at the central military prison. And then there is an attached handwritten note as well. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, I just bring you back to this document because it's essentially where we left off yesterday and I wanted to suggest to you, sir, if I didn't already, the release of the prisoners that's reported by Mr. Bozic in this document, sir, would you agree with me that this was done or appears to have been done in order to enable these gentlemen to go, take part in military operations, use on the front line, as is indicated in this report from Mr. Bozic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not agree with you, Mr. Prosecutor. I first saw this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall if in fact combat operations took place in Rastani, the region around Djubrani that you spoke of yesterday in your direct, whether combat operations occurred up there in the two to three days following the 21st of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember that there was fighting during those days in the area of Rastani and Djubrani.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So if I understand your testimony, sir, you don't know whether these men went up to fight in Rastani or whether they went -- whether they were released for some other reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, I first hear from you that they were in Rastani, in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is P619.1. Witness, if you would just take a moment to look at that, does this appear to be another report made by Mr. Stanko Bozic? Does this appear to be another one of the documents or reports made by Mr. Stanko Bozic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously, he did submit this report, Stanko Bozic did, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next exhibit is P620.2. Witness, as you look at that, my first question again will be whether this appears to be a report or a document made by Stanko Bozic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please allow me to read this first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Take your time. Does this appear to be another report made by Mr. Stanko Bozic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't see the stamp here but it says underneath, Stanko Bozic. Mr. Bozic's name is there. This is the first time I see this report, today. Well, possibly, possibly it could have been him and then on the other hand, it could not have been him, because this is the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a couple of questions about this document. In about the fourth paragraph from the beginning, there is a reference to a private prison in Djubrani. Did you know anything about a private prison in Djubrani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first hear about that private prison here today, and I do not believe that such a prison existed and I never heard that during the war, any kind of private prison existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, the next sentence relates to an order by Mr. Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, regarding detainees released for the requirements of the front line. Would you agree with me, sir, that this statement would appear to relate back to the earlier document that we were looking at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I please go back to the previous document and comment on that first? And then I'll deal with this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: 607.2. Is that not the document you wanted? Witness, if I could Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. just stop you there --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My question was whether the reference in 620.2 is, in fact, a reference to this document, 607.2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not the document that was shown to me. Can I see the document that is addressed to the military court? Because these two documents are interrelated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document -- I mean I can only say, it is not clear to me how Mr. Naletilic can give orders to Mr. Bozic when Mr. Naletilic did not hold any kind of command position in that period, or is there any order in writing on the basis of which Mr. Bozic could write such a report? That is one thing. Now for something else: It says here, "In view of the needs on the front line, defending the city".

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, let me interrupt. What's the number of the document you're looking at now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of the document is 729/93.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay for the record, that's Exhibit P619.1. You can go ahead and say what you wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: So Mr. Naletilic could not command Mr. Bozic. There is no logic in that. Secondly, it says here, "In accordance with first defence line requirements, the following detainees have been released, who are at present members of the Convicts Battalion." [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted] The third illogical point is that the Convicts Battalion was never in the sector of the town defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So what you're saying, sir, is that these reports by Mr. Bozic, you can't explain why he's writing the things that he's writing in these reports, is that basically what you're trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wish to say that these reports of Mr. Bozic's are illogical reports to me, because there is no logic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And they are illogical because they are based on things you didn't know were taking place or didn't think could have been taking place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such things could not have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Next exhibit is 663.1. Sir, this is a document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could we have a redaction on page 14, line 23 and 24? Where it starts out, "Since I"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My question, sir, is again, isn't it true that in fact the Convicts Battalion did, and in fact could, and did in fact avail itself, taking prisoners from the central military prison for the use of its own purposes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you see on this document, sir, in the bottom, it indicates the commander of the Kaznjenicka Bojna as being Mr. Mladen Naletilic, Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here, "Please provide six prisoners to work at the Zeljko Bosnjak ATG, anti-terrorist group based in Ljubuski, commander" it says, "Mladen Naletilic, Tuta." This document has three illogical points about it. First of all, it has to do with the ATG Zeljko Bosnjak. Secondly, the name of Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, is there. As far as people know, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, did not hold any command position at that time. Thirdly, as far as I can see, if I can see this right, it was signed by Mr. Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I don't think we disagree on that last point. It was signed by Mr. Andabak, over the name of Mr. Naletilic, Tuta. Sir, do you have any reason to disagree that in fact these prisoners, these six prisoners, were in all likelihood released to the Zeljko Bosnjak ATG in accordance with this request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if they were handed over. I just see that there is a request here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, the ATG Zeljko Bosnjak, just as equally as the ATG Vinko Skrobo or Benko Penavic, the ATG Zeljko Bosnjak could have requested and used prisoners on an equal basis as other ATGs. Would you agree with me on that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I can agree as far as my own zone of responsibility is concerned. ATG Vinko Skrobo and ATG Benko Penavic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll take your answer on that, sir. The next exhibit is 595.2. It's in folder number 6. As you look that over, sir, does this appear to be a report of Stanko Bozic dated 10 September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a report of Mr. Bozic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And is this the kind of -- sorry, in your direct, you said, and even in your cross yesterday, you said that from time to time you received reports from Mr. Bozic about adverse conditions for the detainees. Does this appear to be such a report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is such a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I notice that here you're indicated as one of the persons to whom this report was directed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said yesterday, and I say the same thing today, whenever I would get such a report from Mr. Bozic, I would immediately take measures. I would investigate the matter that he had referred to. As for all the perpetrators of violations of certain legal regulations, we would impose sanctions on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Exhibit P745, please. I believe this one is already in evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: As you look over that document, Witness, I want to ask you first if you know the person whose name appears at the bottom of the first page, Marijan Biskic. Do you know who that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know him superficially.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: He was an official of the military police for the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, just looking this document over, sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, actually, I don't know whether he worked for the military police or the security service, but for a while, he was involved in one of the two, but I don't know exactly which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in this report, sir, I want to take you to the first page of the report, which is a report on the situation at the Heliodrom, KRZ, which I believe is central military remand prison, dated 3 February, 1994. The second paragraph of this makes reference to the taking of 60 prisoners from the prison, on the basis of a request issued by you, and skipping down a few lines, indicating that these prisoners were returned to the prison on the 29th of January, 1994, three of them were missing, Elmir Jazvin, who was killed, Elvedin Obradovic and Osman Elezovic, who were both wounded and taken to hospital. Do you recall that this -- that these men were wounded and this gentleman was killed while they were out on work detail requested by you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first time I see this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know if any measures were taken to investigate the circumstances under which Elmir Jazvin was killed while working?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said to you, Mr. Prosecutor, that this is the first time I see this document. This document is something I'm quite unfamiliar with. I told you something yesterday and I'm telling you again today. Whenever I would receive a report about such matters, I would always have an investigation carried out, and those who are responsible for certain things would have sanctions imposed against them. But as you can see this document was not addressed to me at all. You can see in the letterhead, at the very beginning of the document on the left-hand side, who the document was addressed to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am afraid that there is a big problem with this document, not to use other language. This document is dated the 3rd of February, 1993, and the source, the Prosecutor says, is Zagreb archives. It is not visible at all here. Thirdly, I have no guarantee that page 09 is part of page 110, that 110, 111, 112 and 113 are integral parts of that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, thank you very much for pointing the problems of this document out. But Mr. Krsnik, as we have said before, you have some -- if you have some problems with the document, you may raise it during the time when we are admitting this document into the evidence rather than at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honour. My concern is invariably, Your Honours, I mean I understand that none of us here would allow ourselves to bring in a document and then examine witnesses concerning such documents if we do not know the origin. However, there has to be some kind of foundation for this. There has to be grounds for this. Because otherwise I could write a document myself and say, "Yes, I got this from such and such a person et cetera." Of course this is an exaggeration but what is the guarantee that this is a truthful document? And we are conducting an examination on the basis of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, this document is an admitted document which came from the Zagreb archive, I believe. Maybe I could give the floor to Mr. Stringer to brief us on the origin of this document at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. First of all, and I don't know whether Mr. Krsnik misspoke or whether there was an interpretation problem, the document is date the 3 February, 1994, not 1993, which is what the record -- or the transcript indicates. It is a document that comes from the Zagreb archive. It is admitted into evidence and therefore would have been one of the documents that was among those submitted under the testimony of Mr. Marko Prelec, who this Trial Chamber heard from a couple of times, during the Prosecution case in chief. I believe beyond the indicia of authenticity, which attached to its having come from the Zagreb archive, I think in going through this, there are other features of it which are consistent with other things we know and are reading, which is what the purpose of asking this witness questions about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, it is not the intention for this Trial Chamber to discuss the document in front of the witness. You have the full right to raise your objections to this Trial Chamber, and even to the appeal court. There is a lot of remedies on your side, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honour. I'm just trying to say that if it's the Zagreb archives, then there would have to be a stamp. And I do not see a single stamp on a single copy and that's what seems strange to me. And also, if we recall, Mr. Prelec's testimony, then we know how these documents got into the archives and through which intelligence services.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think your objection is registered in the transcript but Mr. Krsnik, would you please make sure that you do not raise this kind of objection when the witness is still here? We will give Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you the opportunity to do that. Mr. Stringer. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, just one more question about this document, moving down on the second page of the report, there is a reference here to the 22nd of September, 1993, just before the Muslim attack on Rastani. Do you see that? Mr. Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer, the interpreters could not catch it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could I ask you just to repeat your answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have already said, Mr. Prosecutor, that this is a report that I do not know of. This is the first time I see it. And as it can be seen here, this report was never addressed to me. Everything I see here is unfamiliar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My question, sir, is whether, in fact, the Convicts Battalion did have the authority and the ability to take prisoners from the Heliodrom? We've looked together at a series of documents on this subject, tracing all the way back into that logbook entry that we looked at yesterday regarding the Kaznjenicka Bojna. So my question, sir, is whether, in fact, the Convicts Battalion could take prisoners from the Heliodrom just like all the other units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, Mr. Prosecutor, I said that this is what you inferred. I can only talk about units in my area of responsibility. I do not know, and I do not believe, that the Convicts Battalion could have taken prisoners from the Heliodrom, because the Heliodrom was not within my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is P705.1, the next folder, number 7. While that's coming, sir, I want to ask you a question about an incident you may recall. Do you recall, sir, that on approximately the 24th of November, 1993, members of the Convicts Battalion came into the mechanical engineering faculty, which I believe was in fact your headquarters, led by Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, they were looking for someone named Robert Nosic. Do you remember that incident, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not remember that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's your testimony, sir, you know nothing about an attempt on the part of Mr. Naletilic and the Convicts Battalion to remove Mr. Nosic from the custody of the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember anything in relation to that incident. I did once hear something, but I do not really remember what, and all that I would tell you would be pure guess because there were too many things that happened during that wartime to remember all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, this document, sir, is a report made by Mr. Marinko Zovko, of the first light assault Military Police Battalion. Does that appear to be what this document is, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, evidently this document existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 608. Sir, just --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just say in relation to this document, this document is not addressed to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we go into private session just for a brief moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Then it continues that in the evening of the same day, Mr. Mico Lasic and you went to Siroki Brijeg together. Moving on to the next page, it says, "After all the delays and the start of the operation, the attack began at exactly 1200 hours on September 17th, 1993." And then at the bottom of the report, under the category of "opinion and evaluation of the SIS officer," it says that the sector had received an order from HVO Main Staff to make plans but did not submit any plan for approval with a description and starting time of the operation. So that the order for the attack was issued without the knowledge of the Main Staff. Now, witness, I just want to put this to you because yesterday in your direct testimony you said Mr. Naletilic had no authority to plan military operations in Mostar. Isn't it true, sir, that the events of September 17th, 1993, military operations which occurred on that day, were the result of planning carried out -- and were carried out on the authorisation of Mr. Naletilic after he conferred with you, Vinko Martinovic, and other members of the ATG groups and that all of you carried out these operations without the knowledge or final approval of the HVO Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, this report reeks of insinuation, lies and groundless allegations. This report is completely untrue, and I do not understand what were the prejudices nourished by this gentleman who could have written such a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is Exhibit 456.2. Is this a report of one of your subordinates, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the name of this soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Does it appear to be a report addressed to the commander of the 1st Battalion of the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This report is addressed to the commander of the 1st Battalion of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And the next exhibit, please, 456.1. My question, sir, is whether 456.1 is a report made by you, based on the information received in the previous document from one of your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These reports are compiled by operations duty officers and I did sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And in this report, sir, you refer to the incident which I believe you testified about on your direct exam, in which a patrol from your unit was sent after receiving a report that Muslims were being expelled, they found Stela there with around 40 well-armed soldiers, and said that they were acting on Tuta's orders. Is that what it says in your report, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report, which was put together by the duty officer, says that, but let me answer this question. Yesterday, I explained to Mr. Seric and all of you, Your Honours, that in the city of Mostar, there were cases --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I hate to interrupt you. I know that yesterday you explained that there were people going around claiming that others were calling themselves members of these units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it would be fair and just if the Prosecutor bothered to hear the answers and, Your Honours, to hear the answers, when it comes to such important questions rather than pursue his own course. I don't know how many documents have been used up with this witness. So I think that the witness should be allowed to answer this document just as he did in the case of all the previous documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll give some time to this witness to answer this question but, Witness, you have to be very concise on this point because we have heard your direct examination yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, before he begins could I just say I've got one last document and probably two more questions after this. I know we are right at the break but I want the Court to know that I'm very close to the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You can give the Trial Chamber now your explanation about this report. Before you do so, sir, let me just verify again this is a report signed by you, 456.1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I signed this report, and I'm not denying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the Trial Chamber said that you can go ahead and give an explanation about this document. So please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yesterday, I already set out to explain the situation like this one and similar situations, and now when I see this document, I recall an event when it was reported that Mr. Martinovic, with some of the men in his unit, was expelling civilians, but I went to check that straight away because members of the 1st Battalion are mostly people who are not from Mostar, and who do not know Mr. Martinovic. And with that patrol, and another squad of the military police, I went first to that locality where I did not find anyone, then I went to Mr. Martinovic's headquarters, where the policemen who were on the patrol at the time Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. confirmed that Mr. Martinovic was not the same person as the one who had introduced himself as Martinovic at that time. And Mr. Martinovic at that time was engaged in changing the shifts for the front line, and in that neighbourhood, it was not his men at all and I also received SIS reports several times, which also warned of impersonations. Another thing: This report, I immediately put aside, because we established that what it said was not true and as you can see, the report was typed on the 14th of June and I don't understand how could it then be sent on the 17th, because reports are sent every day. Presumably, one of my duty officers found this report lying on somewhere and sent it not knowing that it had been put aside, shelved as incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object to the speculation that's in the last. I know it's my question but I think at this stage the witness is speculating how the report may have gotten out. The next exhibit is 620.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a SIS report dated 1 October, 1993, regarding abduction of Muslims from Centar II suburb on 29 September, 1993. Now, according to this report, sir, on or around the 29th of September, 1993, Mr. Vinko Martinovic came looking for you at the Mostar defence sector, he was unable to find you, and he then continued and met with the deputy commander of the 1st Light Assault Battalion. An operation was then planned and carried out in which Muslims were rounded up and expelled from Centar II neighbourhood on the 29th of September. The last paragraph of this, sir, says that the commander of the Mostar defence sector was also informed of this operation subsequently, and Colonel Ivan Andabak was informed as well. My question, sir, is whether in fact you were informed of the activities of Mr. Martinovic, Stela, in expelling Muslim persons from the Centar II neighbourhood of Mostar on 29 September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say once again that this report is incorrect, false. I don't know what drove its author to write it. If a gentleman wrote such reports, then they had legal right to punish and start proceedings against anyone, but to write such insinuations, as said, and such lies is beyond me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, did Vinko Martinovic, Stela, regularly engage in ethnic cleansing of Muslims from West Mostar during the time that you held your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vinko Martinovic never participated in the ethnic cleansing of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My last question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, I understand that subsequently you were promoted and became a general. I apologise. I think we need private session for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have to make a break, so we will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, your re-examination? Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, Mr. Seric will start.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Mr. NO, during the cross-examination, you said that various groups misrepresented themselves as being the Tutici and Stelici. I would like to refer to the binder provided by the gentleman from the OTP. I would like document P626 to be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an extra copy of our own, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that you received information from the SIS. Is this one such piece of information? Could you please take a look at the first paragraph, sentence number 3? Could you please read that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The members of these groups are calling out each other's names too loud, and namely the members of these groups call out amongst each other too loudly, the names of their belonging to units such as, for example, Tutici, Stelici, Benkici and so on in order to shift the blame to the wrong address".

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Is this one such information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, I'm going to ask you -- I would like to ask you to look at document 666.2 and I'm actually referring to 468.5. If we could please have the assistance of the usher? It's from the big binder, this one, the big one, the first document, it is P6 -- it is 566.2. If it's easier for you, I can give it to the witness. I'm already prepared. I have the page and all that. Now, the number of the page. In the upper right-hand corner, the last four digits are 4685. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: There are 22 names here. Could you please read them out? It says "convicts" in the form of an adjective, so I don't know what that means, and could you please read out the names? And could you tell me whether there are any Muslim names or is it all Croats?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You don't have to read it out loud. You can just read it and then tell me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, possibly one or two names could be Muslims judging by the last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What about the rest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to move on to another document, 602.1. While we are waiting for the document I'm going to ask you something else. This report of Mr. Stanko Bozic, with the exception of those that were sent to you, did you ever see them before? Can you say anything about these reports?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw them before, and of course, I can't make any comments with regard to reports I'd never seen because I don't know whether they are authentic or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 620.1 [In English] .2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you talking Mr. Krsnik about 620.1 or 620.2?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honour, Judge Diarra, maybe I misspoke. I'm referring to 620.1 and 620.2. I would just like to have something else prepared for me so that we don't have to wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So what have you got in front of you, 620.what, which document are you looking at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at document -- well, I haven't got the number either, like the one you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Oh, yes, it's not there in the Croatian language.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: 620.1 in English, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is that a report dated the 1st of October and the information is entitled "A"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be so kind as to tell me whether you ever saw such reports and what does NN at the bottom mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said to the Prosecutor that this is the first time I see this report. This report is full of insinuations, lies, and I don't know what NN thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What does NN mean? Who is NN?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me it means two letters, N, N. Also, secondly, forwarded to, what does this mean, the HR HB? Is there not a single administration, there is not a single institution that was called the HR HB administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's precisely what I wanted to ask you about. Is there at all an institution called the administration of the HR HB? I would kindly ask the interpreters to help me now. I don't know English that well. What does administration mean? Does it actually mean administration?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that it can also be interpreted as department.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This is what it says quite literally forwarded to the administration of the HR HB. It would be a department, an office, if I understand things correctly. [In English] A department. [Interpretation] I thank the interpreters for their assistance. So this organ, this authority, that is called the Uprava of the HR HB, the department of the HR HB, did it ever exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This name is quite unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Of course I'm not asking you to speculate in any way, and I see that it also says, "The centre of the SIS in Mostar." What was the SIS? Please tell the Honourable Judges?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SIS was the security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This information A, was it written by the so-called sources or rather informants or did the SIS receive this and did they analyse it then? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who would present this kind of information, this group of false information. I don't know who could have written this. However, if a literate person from the SIS wrote this, the SIS did have the authority to investigate this and to process it further.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. You said that this is the first time you see this document today so it is pointless basically to examine you with this document. However, did you hear of any such incident? Perhaps this would be a sensible question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lawyer, I have answered you several times, now that this report is full of falsehoods, full of lies and the whole thing is quite inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Please, let us move on to report 620.2. Have you got it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please tell me who this was sent to, whether you ever saw this document before, and whether there is anything at all that you can say about this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was not sent to me. This is the first time I see this document. And I cannot say a thing about this document because these are things that I am totally unaware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you have already said this to the Prosecutor, and now I'm just going to ask you once again, in this document, is there something important that is missing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, stamps were affixed to documents, and there is not a single stamp on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. I'm not going to waste time now and I'm not going to go through all the documents. So those documents that were not forwarded to you are documents, that you did to the see and they are addressed to you and the Prosecutor showed you dozens of such reports, especially from Mr. Bozic. Had you ever seen them before, apart from now in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had never seen them before. I had seen those that had been addressed to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And now I would like to ask you in conclusion, this would be document 745. Could you please look at page 1, please? Could you please be so kind as to read what it says here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what does it say then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: For Brigadier Marijan Biskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What does that mean for brigadier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody signed this and the signature is illegible and it was signed on behalf of Mr. Biskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is this you are assumption or do you know that he wrote it for Mr. Biskic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that Mr. Biskic knew about it. I said that he signed it on his behalf, this person did, and it says "for", F-O-R.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, this statement, does it have any signature or any identification in terms of who compiled it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [In English] I don't have any further questions, Your Honour. Thank you very much [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from the Judges? Judge Clark?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I established that Vinko Martinovic never expelled Muslims, that is his unit. When we received the report, I went to the site with a patrol which was on duty then, and military policemen who were on the spot at the time when these things were reported, confirmed that those were not the same individuals, that those were different individuals. I wish to say on this occasion, with your leave, that it was not only those criminals who posed as Vinko Martinovic, Stela, or Tuta's boys, they sometimes said they were members of military police or some other units in the town. Furthermore, these criminals did not only expel or plunder Muslims, they also plundered Croats, and I want to point -- to single out two examples here. Between Siroki Brijeg and Mostar, there are three or four villages with a Muslim civilians, and over a thousand Muslim civilians there during the war in those villages, we had our military police checkpoints, civilian, so that nobody would harm those Muslim civilians in any way, and they were there during the war. And the town was large so it was difficult to cover it all, especially since a large number of military police members who were to perform military police tasks, had to cover the front -- the defence line, so that we did not have a sufficient number of policemen to carry out military police duties. We had to see to the curfew. We manned standing and mobile checkpoints, and in this chaos produced by war, we exerted ourselves to stop and prevent those wrongful actions, those crimes, but Croat, Muslim Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and Serb flats were equally looted. Your Honours, I wish to point at one example. When a group of criminals stopped, intercepted two buses with Croats -- it happened on a mountain between Mostar and Jablanica, they stepped into the buses, there were mostly women and children in them, and elderly. These criminals got on to the buses, demanded that those civilians turn over to them all their personal affairs, money, jewellery and the rest, and an old woman stood up and said to them, "Men, please, this is all we have, our houses were burned down. All that we have fits into these bags that we have with us." But they were superior and they had their rifles, and they seized things. And when the old woman realised that they were Croats, she said to them, "Children, my sons, we are Croats too." And one of that group answered, "Sit down, old hag. Nobody is asking you if you are a Croat or a Muslim. This is plunder, not the population census." And I mention this example only because I wanted to tell you that these criminals did not care whether they were dealing with Croats or Muslims or Serbs. Their priority was to line their pockets regardless of the suffering and ordeal of people. And we were doing our utmost to prevent that. I grant there could have been mistakes possibly. I made some mistakes but believe me these mistakes were not deliberate. I could have done something wrong only out of ignorance. But never deliberately. Thank you for allowing me to make such a long answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judges questions? Mr. Seric? Mr. Krsnik? Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, thank you. Further cross-examination by Stringer:

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness in response to Judge Diarra's question about this report received, the incidents in which Muslims were being expelled, you said that you went to the site with a patrol. I'd like to briefly ask you to looks at Exhibits 456.1 and 456.2, which are the two reports about this incident. They would be at the end of the materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour, my apologies to my learned friend but 456.1 and 456.2, the Prosecutor used both these documents in his cross-examination, and extensively so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can answer. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe so, but there are some questions out of Judges' questions. The Prosecutor has the right to confirm certain points in those documents. Yes, you may proceed, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness, 456.2, the first one I want to look at. Now, this is a report, sir, from Zovko, Romeo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it is.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: It says after I sent the men to the line, I went to the command of the 1st Battalion." That's where he received the report about this incident, I believe. He says, "I went, I immediately went to the scene and encountered Stela with 40 soldiers." Now isn't it true, sir, that Mr. Zavko, Romeo would have known Stela and would have been able to positively identify Stela as the person involved in these activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is a speculative one and he is -- a speculative answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. Romeo could not have known Stela.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Why not? How is it possible that he didn't know Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because when I asked him later on whether he had ever seen Mr. Stela before, his answer was that he had not.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Now, I notice in this report, sir, he does not say that he went to the scene and encountered people who identified themselves as Stela or Stela's men. He says it's Stela.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he could put it that way but after the report, when I came to the battalion, together with this patrol, I went to the site and I did not see Stela there. After that, I went to the command, where Mr. Martinovic was about to change a shift, and where the relevant gentleman from the police who were there at the time said that the person who had introduced themselves -- himself as Stela, and now that they were standing in front of Mr. Stela, that those two were not one and the same person.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: The other exhibit is 456.1. This is the report signed by you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And in this report, sir, you say, "Around 1630 hours, we received a report of uniformed men were rounding up Muslim civilians in the Dum block. A patrol was sent to the site where they found Stela." Now the fact is, sir, a patrol was sent to this site and you didn't go, you did not go out to check out these reports personally. Isn't that true? A patrol was sent out and the findings of the patrol are contained in the other document, 456.2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I am not the one who writes this report. I am not saying that I sent a patrol. This report was put together by the duty officer who had received a report, and when the duty officer notified me, I went after that. That is after this thing that the report talks about, and one can see it from this report. I cannot report that I met my assistant, seeing that I'm his superior.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Sir, my point is this: The report you signed, I assume you wanted to make an accurate report, a full report, and that you don't say anywhere in this report that you in fact went personally to the scene. And that's because you didn't go to the scene, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the scene after the report, and I stayed this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for coming here to give your evidence. We appreciate it very much. When the usher pulls down the blinds, she will show you out of the room. All of us wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I thank you for allowing me to come to this Tribunal and tell the truth. Thank you once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, are there any documents to tender at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but I finished one notebook yesterday and I brought my new one. I'd like to put it in writing, if you will allow me that. I'll file it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, tomorrow. And I guess there are a lot of documents on the Prosecution side. I believe that within a certain period of time, you will submit your written applications for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We will do that before the end of this week, Mr. President. Probably tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we would like to tender D226, that is the photograph which was marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I guess there is no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: None, Mr. President, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So this photograph is admitted into evidence. Mr. Krsnik, are there any protective measures for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, face distortion and a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I guess there is no objections from the Prosecution side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your request is granted. Could we have the next witness, please, Madam Usher?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would like to warn the Judges that the transcript disappeared from the screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about the both parties? Do you have the transcript on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we still have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In this case, I think we will proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you all right? Make yourself comfortable, don't sit too far away from the microphone. But make yourself at home and now look at the monitor in front of you, and I will now give you some instructions as I do with every witness. The chief problem is interpretation. I suppose this is the first time that you are in a situation like this. So try, please, to focus and don't be either too fast or too slow. So that the interpreters could interpret what you say and you can see on your screen a dot which moves. When you see it stopped, that is perhaps the best time when you should start answering.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, the usher will show you a piece of paper with your name. Don't say it aloud. Just tell us if indeed that is your name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So with my first team I arrived in Mostar in the early morning hours. I reported to Brigadier Mica Lasic, who informed me that there was an attack by Muslims in Mostar and that I should go towards Vranica and Djacki Dom together with my team, because according to this order, the Muslim forces from the Rondo wanted to meet with the command of the 4th Corps that was at the building at Vranica. After about an hour or so, the rest of the members of my unit started coming in and then I had them deployed there. Also, because we were not familiar with Mostar, we had with us a platoon from the 3rd Brigade, and as a reserve, we had Juka Prazina's unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, now that we have touched upon Mr. Juka Prazina. Do you know anything about him, who he was, what kind of unit that was, who was his commander? Please go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: That was the first time I saw Juka Prazina in my life, is the first time I saw him live, but I had seen him on television, because he was famous for his participation in the defence of Sarajevo. As far as I know, he was a kind of ATG too or some kind of a special unit, and he was more or less supposed to operate the way I was supposed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, what was your task and what happened afterwards on that day, the 9th of May? Just to help the Honourable Judges, could you please explain your task? Could you say what exactly happened? I don't want to interrupt you. Could you please just tell the Honourable Trial Chamber about what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: My first task was to stop the attack, and if the situation was right, I should launch a counterattack. Of course, all of this was made more difficult because already from the early morning hours, there were masses of civilians in Mostar who were fleeing from their houses and their apartments. Because there was shooting all over. People who lived nearby, as a matter of fact, told me that from the building at Vranica they killed, I don't know I'm not sure, a civilian or a military policeman of the HVO. But I'm not sure about that because I hadn't arrived then. We managed to prevent their break through and also the joining of their forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you have direct combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Fighting in a built-up area is the most difficult kind of combat operation. There is no classical line of separation or a classical front, as elsewhere. Civilians constitute a major problem because they move about a lot as they are fleeing from the fire. Again, it makes it possible for all the parties involved to let their own sabotage and diversion units into the picture. So fighting usually took place at a distance between 10 and 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please tell us about this action? You were deployed around Vranica and then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: At first, we stopped the -- and prevented the penetration from the Rondo to Vranica, and then we fully blocked the command, the headquarters, of the 4th Corps, and we were asking the members of the army to surrender. They didn't want to surrender, and then indeed, heavy fighting ensued. People were not shooting only from the positions that had already been taken but also from all floors in the building. So we also had quite a few casualties. People were not only wounded but were even killed. The fighting went on for two days. On the second day, somewhere around noon, they did surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, so please let's clarify this, your unit was the one that -- I don't know how to put this, I'm looking for the right expression, you're unit was the one that was engaged in the fighting around Vranica, and also this platoon that you mentioned, the local forces, that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you see any other unit, together with you, in this action of Vranica or whatever I should call it, for example the Convicts Battalion or Mr. Mladen Naletilic, on that date, the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please tell us when this action was completed, whether there were any members of the BiH army that were taken prisoner and what happened to these prisoners, if any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: There were two groups of prisoners. One group was taken prisoner on the 9th, I think. Those are the ones that were supposed to link up with the Rondo. We got them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. I know that the Honourable Trial Chamber knows a lot about Mostar already. I have a map here so that when you're talking about the Rondo and this linking up, let us ask Madam Registrar to give us this map, 11.8, I think. Sorry, it is 11.18, is could we have it put on the ELMO so the Honourable Trial Chamber could take a look at this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Rondo is a roundabout in Mostar, and the attempt to link up went along this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell me now, when this action was completed, when these people were taken prisoner, what happened to them? That is where we broke off.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: This first group of prisoners were taken prisoner during the combat action. We pulled them out of the zone where we were facing each other and where there was shooting. We handed them over and we returned and immediately proceeded with the combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was it always that way? Did you always hand over your prisoners when you took them? You said you handed them over but you didn't say to who. And was this the case with all special units and all ATGs if you did have any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Yes. We had no conditions to keep prisoners or did we have the authorities that would carry out a proper interrogation, and usually they were handed over either to higher commands or to the military police or -- or to a different line that was behind us, to the reserve or -- because we could not take care of them if we were combat-active.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please finish answering this question and then we are going to take a break. All right you had a group of prisoners taken on the 9th. And then what about the 10th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: On the 10th, I think there were about 40 or so persons, I don't know exactly, from the headquarters at Vranica and I went to the headquarters building to see whether there were any Claymore mines or anything like that in order to prevent any kind of surprise. Mr. Prazina led them. And after that, I found him in front of the building of the ministry, together with these prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please point out on the map where this building of the ministry was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Approximately around here, you can't really see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. Now we have to take a break, Mr. Witness, and now that we will be going outs, you have a magic marker there and you can just put a circle around where the building of the ministry was and then we can take the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Your Honours, this would be the right time to take a break, wouldn't it?
