utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. Krsnik, please continue, but bear in mind that we will break 20 minutes early so as to accommodate the request from Defence council to participate in the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean at 1.25, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we broke off when you started explaining Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the map of Mostar, and you put that little cross there, and could you please put M.O., to denote Ministarstvo Obrane, meaning "Ministry of Defence"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were all the prisoners brought there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did they go to any other location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to say then what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Krsnik, I was just reading the notes to see if I made a mistake and I notice what you're saying now, you're talking about 10th of May, but just before the break, you were talking about prisoners who had been taken on the 9th of May, the ones who didn't link up, the ones from the Rondo who didn't link up. How have we taken a jump from those prisoners to the ones on the 10th of May? I think you need to cover some other ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour, but the witness really explained this very nicely. I don't know what the transcript says but the witness explained that during the fighting on the 9th they took prisoners, some people who wanted to link up with Vranica, and then they took them prisoner handed them over to the military police and then they went on fighting. I thought that this was clear but if not, perhaps I should clarify it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: We just don't know where the other 40 prisoners came from. Suddenly he sees Mr. Prazina standing outside a building with 40 prisoners without any information about where those prisoners came from and assuming that they are not the same prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, you've heard the Honourable Judge and that is why we are trying to explain things to our Honourable Trial Chamber as best we can so please bear in mind the fact that the Honourable Judges and many other people were not there then. So tell us again, who brought the prisoners, from where, when, happened on the 9th, what happened on the 10th, let's give a full explanation to the Honourable Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: On the 9th, there was a smaller group of prisoners. They were taken out of the zone of combat operations. They were handed over and taken for further interrogations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what about the 10th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: On the following day, from the command of the 4th Corps, there was this other, bigger group of prisoners. While I was searching the premises of the 4th Corps, Juka Prazina took them to the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what happened to them then, in front of the ministry? Were you in front of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Yes. I came in front of the ministry. I saw a big group of civilians and soldiers. I saw these prisoners, and Juka Prazina arguing with one of these prisoners. As a matter of fact, he wanted to hit him but I wouldn't let him do it. And I said to him that he should escort them to the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did he escort them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: I think he did escort them because after that I handed over the documentation that was also seized, and I got approval to move my forces towards Capljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, on that day, on the 10th of May, in front of the ministry, did you see Mr. Mladen Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, when did he come, if you know, and were you with him all the time? Why did he come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: That's a lot of questions, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm sorry. So first of all, were you with him all the time? Did you see when you -- did you see him when he came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: I said that. When I saw Juka Prazina clamouring there, I set out towards him. He was on one side. And when I talked to him, then Mr. Naletilic came up to me and asked me how I had fared. Not referring to me personally but to the unit, whether there were any casualties, there were people who were wounded or killed, and he showed particular interest in a few guys who were from Siroki Brijeg and who were in my unit. Then I said to him that two of my men were wounded in the spine and were therefore 100 per cent disabled. And then we proceeded to walk towards the building of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Mladen Naletilic hit anyone over there or talk to anyone there, talk to any one of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: No, he certainly did not hit anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What was he wearing then? I know this was ten years ago but do you remember maybe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: He was dressed sort of half-half. It was either trousers and a top, I don't know, I think he had a civilian T-shirt on and camouflage trousers or the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was it a short-sleeved T-shirt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Yes, it was a short-sleeve T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, to the best of your knowledge, did Mladen Naletilic command anyone of the units that was involved in the fighting in Mostar on the 9th and 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you perhaps hear Mladen Naletilic issuing orders to anyone when you were there with him in front of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did the two of you part that day in front of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Yes. I went into the ministry building and he proceeded towards his car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did anybody else abuse the prisoners who were members of the BH Army in your presence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: There were insults and swear words by the people who were gathering around there, but apart from that attempt made by Juka Prazina, I didn't see anybody else do that. And Juka also wanted to hit some man because I guess they were friends. I don't know exactly. He said something like, "Is this the way you betrayed me, brother?" Or something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We heard some testimonies here, so I am asking you therefore whether any of the prisoners were killed in front of the ministry building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was anybody shot in the head there in front of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Nobody would probably survive being shot in the head but no, nobody was shot in the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did Mr. Naletilic take his pistol out? Did he shot at anyone? Did he have a weapon at all? Do you remember any of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: I do not remember whether he had a pistol, but he didn't take it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who took prisoner these members of the BH Army in Vranica? What can you tell the Trial Chamber about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: My unit and the unit of Juka Prazina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, were there any units of the Croatian Army there, that is to say units of the army from the Republic of Croatia, of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: There weren't any organised units, established units, but there were many members of the Croatian Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: I mean people who fought in Croatia during the war, and who were born in Herzegovina or in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and they asked to come and they did come to fight. So they either joined some units or they made smaller groups of their own that would then join in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I asked you whether the Croatian Army had officially come in, when I asked you what I asked you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: I think that I answered you. I told you that there weren't any organised or established units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer, too. And my final question: According to what you know, did Mr. Naletilic play any role in the conflict between Croats and Muslims in Herzegovina or rather BH Army or MOS and the HVO in the autumn of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: What role do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I mean a military or political.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: I do not think so, because Mr. -- When he ceased to be the commander of the Convicts Battalion, he remained aside, and what I know, I'm sure he didn't have any role.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. Do you know the front line called Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Yes. I was there once.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. In September, 1993, that is the 23rd of September, 1993, did this front line in Rastani have its commander? If yes, who was it? And is Djubrani a part of the Rastani front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: When I was in Rastani, the commander of that particular sector was Stampar. I think he is a colonel but I'm not sure. But I think that was before that time that you are asking me about. He, however, continued as the commander of the sector because Rastani changed hands often. Djubrani, yes, yes, Djubrani is part of it, and if somebody had enough strength to take Djubrani, he'd also deal with Rastani much easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you tell the Honourable Court, for instance, you come with your unit to Rastani, who do you subordinate yourself to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Well, I'd first say that I received my orders from the Main Staff, and then I'm attached to the commander of the military district, and when he gives me my task and location, then with the commander on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And does that hold true of all the professional units and the ATGs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: That holds true of the professional units. And ATGs mostly worked for some kind of their mother units or locally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. Who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Chief of the Main Staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, this chief of the Main Staff, did he have an assistant for professional -- for the professional units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was that? And when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: It was Mr. Ivica Primorac, and when he left to be trained, I replaced him for a short while in the Ludvig Pavlovic unit and after that it was Mr. Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And after that, when was that when Mr. Andabak took over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Late 1993 or 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Maybe the witness will give the name of Mr. Andabak because we had different Andabaks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, the name Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And could we have now D1/82, please? And this will be my final question, so that you could explain to the Honourable Court this command function. Where are you in this chart? Where is the Convicts Battalion? Where are other ATGs? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you have the translation here on the ELMO, and you can point at individual boxes using the English text but you have the Croatian text in front of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: So my unit would be in this box here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And who else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Ante Bruno Busic regiment, the Convicts Battalion, and Baja Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you referring to 1993 or --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: No, I mean when we were organised in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, please, what happened later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: After that, the three of us, I mean the three professional units, remained, my unit, Bruno Busic, Baja Kraljevic, and parts of the convicts that remained were practically attached to the Siroki Brijeg Brigade, just as some other ATGs were parts of brigades or at various places in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And I'm asking you this because you are a professional soldier. I didn't ask others that. Where would you place the Convicts Battalion? And I'm always talking about April, 1993, end of 1993. Where would you put them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: In view of its strength and its composition it should be either here or here, except that there should be indicated the brigade with which it worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, will you describe it? For instance, you have received summons to go to a front line. Will you now describe this whole -- this whole channel, 1993, how do you go there, who issues you orders, will you describe it? For instance you are called up by the Mostar operative zone and ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: I believe I've already explained it, but I'll repeat it. If operative -- if the Mostar operative zone needs me, then it communicates directly with the Chief of the Main Staff, and he issues me with my task. And I then attach myself, I then resubordinate myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: On the front line where you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Yes, I told you I resubordinated myself to the operative zone because it is the one which asked for my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that is what held true of all the professional units or perhaps ATGs if they were called to act outside their own brigade? Would it be the same channel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: It's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. What about the ATGs would they follow the same channels?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If an ATG is called up, can you explain how did it work then? I mean the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: ATG could also be called up in case of an express need, but the unit which is already active, for instance, Mostar Brigade, be it the 1st, the 2nd or the 3rd or the Siroki Brijeg Brigade one or Capljina, because they did lots of things through them, logistic things and other, because the ATGs had few members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you ever with the ATG Convicts Battalion between May, 1993 and the end? Did you Ludvig Pavlovic know where they were, did you act together in an operation or -- ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: No, we did not carry out any actions jointly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know, did you meet them, say, sometime in May, June, July, August, September, October?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: Most of those good guys that I knew from the Convicts Battalion at the time was with Baja Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We heard, and this is my last question, we also heard some testimony how in the area of Dubrave, Rotimlje, the area of responsibility, you will know better whether it is Kralj Tomislav or something like that, that they were being disarmed and arrested sometime around the 1st of July only because they were Muslims. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP
utterances.text: I know that was the area of responsibilities of the 1st Herzegovina Brigade. And they were disarmed because the weapons had -- because the weapons were targeting the HVO units. I know it because I participated in one such action.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like to distribute the exhibits. Shall I begin?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please. And remember, we only have ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, unfortunately, I can only start my cross-examination now. And I would ask the Trial Chamber to go into a private session for some moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.
